title: The Skin of Others in Your Game
coreMove: Before judging courage, map whose security the actor would burn by telling the truth.
sourcePressure: People often compromise because institutions can punish dependents, families, colleagues, or reputations around them.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making the lesson generic whistleblower sympathy instead of indirect downside transfer.

sourceAnchors.name: whistleblower dilemma
sourceAnchors.detail: The authorized excerpt centers the moral conflict of exposing hidden harm when family security and future income may be destroyed.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The whistleblower is not only risking a job; the mortgage and school fees are also in the room.

sourceAnchors.name: celibacy and financial independence
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar says Taleb treats lack of attachments and financial independence as partial shields against others carrying your downside.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A person with fewer hostage points is harder to own, which is why private obligations can become public leverage.

sourceAnchors.name: suicide terrorist deterrence logic
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar says the chapter closes by asking how to inject real downside into actors who otherwise face no ordinary deterrent.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The extreme case should stay narrow: deterrence fails when the actor has removed ordinary downside from himself.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: pharmaceutical quality analyst considering a safety disclosure
exampleSpecs.audience: employee whose spouse and children depend on her benefits
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients are exposed, but her family would absorb retaliation first
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hannah names each dependent cost on a notepad before deciding how to disclose through a protected channel.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a benefits card beside a deviation report

exampleSpecs.audience: official whose brother works for the contractor
exampleSpecs.stakes: family employment becomes a lever against public duty
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Julien tells his supervisor to remove his brother from the call and files the defect with a witness present.

exampleSpecs.domain: research nurse asked to soften adverse-event language
exampleSpecs.audience: clinical worker whose team would lose funding after a blunt report
